criteria.bundle_handle: Introduce a bundle handle minted by test::evidence_open: blobs go in through test::evidence_append under caller-chosen names, and test::evidence_seal closes the bundle and hands back digests together with a receipt kind drawn from a closed vocabulary. Because the sealed digest covers exactly the appended blobs, stray or substituted files cannot leak into the attested artifact.
criteria.memory_only: Persist nothing from inside the test module: evidence remains ordinary Can values and whatever invoked the test decides how to store them. This adds no operations at all, at the price of no sealed artifact the owner can point at and no shared receipt vocabulary.
criteria.path_seal: Keep writing evidence through the existing files::* operations to arbitrary locations, then call a single new test::evidence_seal over a str[] of paths to obtain digests and a receipt kind. Only one operation is added, but the seal reads whatever paths it is handed, so absent, exchanged, or out-of-scope files surface only at seal time.

evidence_bundle.instructions: How should sealed, digested receipts in the qualified-report, n-receipt, cleanup-receipt vocabulary be produced with the smallest adequate mechanism?

criteria.grant_wrapped_reuse: Keep calling the existing process::run with its free-form executable string, guarded by a fresh test::grant_process check that permits a single call per grant. This adds almost nothing, yet every permitted call may still designate any executable, leaving arbitrary dispatch expressible within an authorized grant.
criteria.keyed_dispatch: Replace the executable path with a tool key: test::run_tool accepts a key the N owner registered for this grant together with argv/cwd/env/options. The owner pre-registers the staged implements (bundled bun, formatter, built CLI); keys outside the registry refuse before any spawn. Each run therefore carries a closed dispatch vocabulary, with workspace-relative staging recorded inside the tool entries.
criteria.workspace_relative: Confine spawning to a workspace: test::process_run accepts a workspace handle and a relative executable path plus argv/cwd/env/options. Absolute paths and ../ escapes refuse; only binaries beneath the sealed workspace root may run. Confinement comes from the handle boundary rather than from a registry.

process_dispatch.instructions: How should test process spawning express staged offline tool runs (cwd/env/argv/limits, descendant cleanup) while leaving arbitrary dispatch/eval unrepresentable?

criteria.no_workspace_ops: Skip workspace operations entirely: tests hand raw paths to files::* and arrange staging and cleanup by discipline. No new mechanism and no confinement either, plus no cleanup receipt the owner can observe.
criteria.opaque_handle: Mint an opaque, non-constructible workspace handle via test::workspace_open, tied to a fresh directory owned by the grant; companion test::* file operations accept the handle with a relative path, and test::workspace_close seals the directory and queues cleanup. Forged handles miss table lookup, stale handles miss liveness lookup, and absolute or escaping paths refuse. This continues the grant/channel handle discipline.
criteria.root_path_string: Return the fresh directory as an ordinary str path from test::workspace_root and keep using the current files::* operations over joined paths. This is a single new operation, but the boundary is advisory: a test may hand files::* any path whatsoever.

workspace_model.instructions: How should tests obtain isolated scratch directories that clean up, without opening ambient file access, using the least sufficient mechanism?
